questions.question:
D1 — Reuse the shared Retry-After parser for the two proposed callers, or copy it locally?
Project/branch/task: gstack-shared-plan-callers fixture, branch main, planning src/import-worker.ts and src/sync-route.ts.
ELI10: Both new files need to turn a Retry-After header into a wait in seconds, exactly the way the scheduler already does. The scheduler already gets that from one tested function in lib/retry-after.ts. The plan instead writes a fresh copy of that logic inside each new file. Copies look identical today but can drift apart silently, so a future fix to one would not reach the others.
Stakes if we pick wrong: with local copies, a later ceiling or date-parsing fix lands in one place and the other callers keep waiting the wrong number of seconds; with reuse but thin proof, callers depend on past-date and date-ceiling behavior that no test pins down.
Recommendation: A because the shared helper already exists, is exercised by the scheduler, and reuse removes about 26 implementation lines while adding only the contract cases the new callers rely on.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=5/10
Pros / cons:
A) Reuse helper, full proof (recommended)
  ✅ Zero new parser logic; both callers import retrySeconds(value, now, fallback) exactly as src/scheduler.ts does today
  ✅ Adds the missing regression cases (past date → 0, date beyond cap → 3600, unsafe integer → fallback, whitespace-only → fallback) to test/retry-after.test.ts, plus one delegation assertion per caller integration test
  ❌ Any future bug in the shared helper now reaches the scheduler and both new callers at once (human: ~1 h / CC: ~5 min)
B) Reuse helper, existing proof
  ✅ Same import wiring as A with no changes to the shared test file
  ✅ Smallest possible diff: roughly two lines per caller plus the integration tests the plan already promises
  ❌ Past-date and date-ceiling paths the callers depend on remain untested, so a regression there would reach production unnoticed (human: ~45 min / CC: ~3 min)
C) Local parser per caller
  ✅ Each caller is fully self-contained and can diverge later without touching shared code
  ✅ No change to lib/retry-after.ts or its test file
  ❌ Adds two more 15-line copies of logic that already exists three times in the repo, each needing its own full contract test to meet the every-behavior-tested bar (human: ~2 h / CC: ~10 min)
Net: trading a slightly larger shared blast radius for one tested source of truth and about 26 fewer implementation lines.

options.label: Reuse helper, full proof
options.description: Both src/import-worker.ts and src/sync-route.ts import retrySeconds from lib/retry-after.ts and call retrySeconds(header, now, fallback); no local parser. Shared contract stays unchanged. Adds four regression cases to test/retry-after.test.ts (past date → 0, date beyond 3600 s cap → 3600, unsafe integer → fallback, whitespace-only → fallback). Each caller's integration test asserts its wait equals the helper's output for an injected now, a null header and one date header. Implementation ≈ +4 lines vs ~30 drafted (saves ~26); tests ≈ +6. Blast radius: scheduler plus both callers. Existing copies in src/retry-route.ts and src/retry-worker.ts stay untouched. (human: ~1 h / CC: ~5 min)

options.label: Reuse helper, existing proof
options.description: Same import wiring as A in both callers, with the same caller integration tests, but test/retry-after.test.ts stays at its current five cases. Shared contract unchanged. Implementation ≈ +4 lines (saves ~26); tests ≈ +2. The past-date → 0, date-ceiling, unsafe-integer and whitespace-only paths remain unpinned by any test. Existing copies stay untouched. (human: ~45 min / CC: ~3 min)

options.label: Local parser per caller
options.description: Keep the plan as drafted: each caller carries its own 15-line copy of the parser matching lib/retry-after.ts byte-for-byte. No change to lib/retry-after.ts or its test. Each caller integration test must also repeat the full contract cases (null, invalid, trimmed digits, cap, date, past date) so each copy is independently pinned. Implementation ≈ +30 lines (saves 0); tests ≈ +16-20. Any future parser fix must be applied to each copy separately. (human: ~2 h / CC: ~10 min)
